Britain's Got Talent: Alison Jiear, Ella Shaw and UDI steal the show while Entity Allstars get Golden Buzzer

Vladimir Georgievsky's trampoline act also had viewers laughing

It’s the fifth week of Britain's Got Talent and what better way to start the episode than with a policeman turned drag queen?

Aaron Carty hit headlines a few years ago when he was snapped arrested late Big Brother contestant, Jade Goody, but now he’s took off his uniform and strapped on a sequinned leotard.

Though Carty isn’t just any drag queen, he’s the Michelle Kelly Beyonce of drag queens as a Beyonce impersonator.

Admittedly, she wouldn’t win any Fishy Awards from RuPaul’s Drag Race, but the dancing wasn’t half bad and so with three yeses, and Simon Cowell’s nod, Aaron was put through to the next round.

Now if a former police officer turned drag queen wasn’t quite your bag, then the next act may have done it for you, because who doesn’t love a balloon-popping dog?

Sassy Aaron blows the Britain's Got Talent audience away

Mitch and Cally The Wonderdog thundered onto the stage with one goal - to break a world record.

Apparently someone, somewhere had already achieved a world record for a dog popping the most balloons and so Mitch and Cally were here to smash that record and advance through Britain’s Got Talent.


“Balloon popping is just her favourite thing in the whole world,” explained Mitch of his long-haired Jack Russell Terrier.

Meanwhile, while Cally was busy running around popping balloons, we met Daniel Crute, who by day is a 40-year-old builder and labourer, but by night is a Victorian Strongman called Leopold Aleksander.


Now, ordinarily, a Victorian Strongman wouldn’t be the most exciting act, but add into it Amanda Holden and a frying pan and you’ve got yourself an act.

Unfortunately, Amanda didn’t seem super thrilled to have her presence requested by a large muscled man holding a recently-crushed frying pan, but in for a penny and all that and up she got onto the stage.

“Good afternoon my dear. If you wouldn’t mind stepping one front in front of the other,” said Leopold.

“Clench my dear, clench,” he added much to the delight of the audience.

Amanda added:“I had fish and chips and sticky toffee pudding for my tea so I think you did very well to lift me. It’s definitely yes from me.”

Watch Ella blow the judges away with her music on Britain's Got Talent

Three more yeses followed and Leopold/Daniel was put through to the next round. Maybe he’ll lift Alesha next time?

But it was then time, via the magic of television, to go back to Cally the Wonderdog’s attempt to break a world record, and possibly her future hearing.

Unfortunately, Cally couldn’t quite pop the full 100 balloons in under 44 seconds, so the judges decided to give her another chance with four yeses. Bless.

From a failure of a dog to a Russian trampoline act, this week’s Britain’s Got Talent is nothing if not varied.

Vladimir Georgievsky is a 45-year-old from Russia, but who moved to Swansea after meeting his wife in a nightclub there.

Vladimir claimed he only started bouncing when he bought a trampoline for his two sons, but it soon became clear that only a brilliant bouncer could bounce quite so badly and make it look hilarious.

That looks sore! Britain's Got Talent trampoline act fall

It was a wonder he didn’t do himself a mischief with all the clattering he did onto that wooden board.

David Walliams: “I think you’re secretly really good at trampolining, aren’t you? That was great and we’re always saying we’re looking for something we’d never seen before and I know Simon would really appreciate the bits where you could have been injured very badly.”

Amanda: “I really enjoyed it because it goes back to the silent movie days. Just shows that a relatively young audience can still appreciate it and still love it.”

Simon: “It was fantastic. I thought it was really really good.”

Alesha: “I think you’d be perfect for the Royal Variety Performance. You choreographed that to perfection.”

It was four yeses for Vladmir.

If there was one way to celebrate your first time out of your home country, then a Britain’s Got Talent audition must be the best way.

It certainly was for 16-year-old student and dancer Dylan Byrd, from County Cavan in Ireland.

His dance moves, surprising as they were, impressed three of the judges, but not Alesha Dixon, who was heavily booed when she hit her buzzer during his audition.

David Walliams: “I absolutely loved it. I guess that’s a lot of practising in front of the bedroom mirror.”

Amanda: “For you to be literally doing this in your bedroom, then got on a plane for the first time, come here and done it in front of all these people, with so much confidence, I just think high five Dylan.”

Alesha: “I think you’re lovely but I didn’t think the dance was the standard that I’m personally looking for and I’m so sorry.”

Simon: “I mean, look, the thing is Dylan, is that I do find a lot of dance acts quite boring but I thought you were great, really fun. I don’t understand why Alesha didn’t get you.”


But then Dylan brought the audience to the brink of tears when he said that he wanted to impress Alesha because she does dancing, leaving Alesha holding her head in her hands and saying: “Oh no.”

Not that it changed Alesha’s mind when it came to the vote, as while the other judges all gave Dylan yeses, Alesha said simply: “I’m so sorry darling, today it’s a no.”

It was like Simon and Alesha had swapped personalities, as then we got a nice segment of Alesha being mean to lots of acts.

But not before David quipped: “Did you leave your job open at Strictly? I mean, can you go back?"

Next up to feel Alesha’s wrath was Joanna Cameron, a comedy hypnotist from Virginia in the US of A. Well why not? We’ve had a hypnotist dog, so we could have a grudge match between then.

Joanna definitely thinks she can win and she attempted to prove it by knocking out half the audience and having them slink down to the floor ‘peacefully, like a horse’.

Finally tiring of the act, Alesha said the act was going to put her to sleep - but not for the right reasons - before hitting her buzzer and shouting ‘WAKEY WAKEY’ at the volunteers on the stage.


And with that Hurricane Alesha swept Joanna off the stage, with no-one or nothing being able to warm her cold, icey heart. UNTIL…

Oh yes, you see Britain’s Got Talent is nothing if not consistent so a run of Alesha hating things can only end one way - I smell a Golden Buzzer.

Entity Allstars are a 20-piece dance troupe from Essex and they feature one person who may or may not be familiar to you, especially if you watch the X Factor.

On last year’s series of ITV’s other Simon Cowell-fronted talent show, there was a contestant called Lauren Platt who came fourth. But with her, she brought her younger brother, who wouldn’t you just know it, was a dancer and quite good.

Not one to miss a trick, Simon told him there and then to audition for BGT next year and he’s here, and he’s brought 19 of his closest friends with him.

X Factor 2014: Lauren Platt's little brother lights up the stage dancing in leather jacket

Well, it didn’t take long for their high-kicking, back-flipping, impeccably choreographed routine to impress, not just the audience, but also the judges and it it had Alesha Dixon hitting that Golden Buzzer before the other judges could even get out their compliments.

Alesha joined the troupe on stage, gushing: “You were so good. You smashed it.”

David Walliams: “You are absolute world class.”

Amanda Holden: “It felt so dynamic and so many dance crews come up here and say, ‘Oh yeah, we’ve got something different and we’ve got nothing’ and you smashed it today.”


Simon Cowell: “And that’s why Great Britain is great. Seriously unbelievable, great choice Alesha. I kinda feel that I’m sort of part of your crew because I did invite you onto the show so I am part of you.”

Alesha Dixon: “I love you guys. Honestly, I think you’re fantastic. The strength and the power and the focus and the determination was superb. You absolutely smashed it.”

And with that, Entity Allstars were through, and it was now time for a change of pace with a DJ.

DJ John is a 45-year-old DJ from Newcastle-upon-tyne who says he auditioned because he’s got a gift.

Entity show off their slick dancing routine

“My dream is to be a star like Ant and Dec and Cheryl Cole,” he told the judges, perhaps not realising that the three people are quite different.

Speaking of quite different, DJ John’s act was certainly something different with him taking to the stage with an act that was a cross between DJing and dancing. Of sorts.

There was a lot of leg brushes, hand-waving, lots of teeth on display, and he got the audience on their feet as if it was some sort of 1980s aerobics class in a provincial gym.

Even Ant and Dec joined him on stage to dance, as Simon Cowell buzzed him off with a mixture of facial expressions.


“You just need to let the beat control your body, Simon. That’s what you need,” said David Walliams before voting to put John through.

Only Simon tried to dash DJ John’s dreams, and then off he popped to the next round.

Now if a DJ who didn’t DJ, or mix, or do anything but run around, wasn’t your thing then Polly Rowley-Sams will be right up your street, for she wrote her own song - about dust.

“Dust. Dust. Dust. Dust. Dust. Dust. Dust. Dust. Dust mites,” she sang like she was something out of Little Britain.

Amanda said she could see what she was trying to do, which probably says more about Amanda and her cleaning habits than anything else, but all was not lost, as Ella Shaw was next.

Ella is an 18-year-old singer from a small village outside of Blackburn and she will also be singing an original song, though thankfully, it’s not about dust.

“I’ve been gigging up and down the country,” Ella explained. "I’ve been doing all the gigs where nobody wants to listen so to perform at the Royal Variety Show in front of the Royal Family would be so amazing.”

“Ever since I was younger my parents have been my cheerleaders, so to speak.

“I just one day want to give it back to them, what they’ve invested in me, the time and everything really.”

Ella took to the stage to sing her original song Summertime and, it’s safe to say it was better than the dust song, judging by the standing ovation and the comments she got.


Alesha Dixon said: “Ella, I love your voice. It was a very subtle, intimate performance and the fact that you’re here doing original material is admirable and I think you’re one to watch.”

David Walliams: “It is very brave to come on and sing an original song. You’re so young and yet you’re already on your way to being a star.”

Amanda Holden: “It’s like a really bright happy voice that you’ve got. It was beautiful.”

Simon Cowell: “You’ve got what I call a very current voice. I think you’re mega, mega talented.”

All that praise and Ella got her four yeses and a place in the next round.

Next up was magician’s assistant Chloe Crawford, who wants to drop the assistant and become the magician.

The 26-year-old from Portsmouth is currently an assistant in Las Vegas, and it’s safe to say she’s wasted as just the damsel in distress.

Hopping onto a motorcycle, she rides it into a cage, that’s then winched to the top off the stage, before exploding and then re-appearing on the other side in a box. It was all very magical.


Alesha: “It’s just so refreshing seeing a beautiful woman doing magic, it’s fantastic.”

Simon: “It’s kinda brought Vegas back to London and I like that and you are someone we’re going to remember.”

And they would, because they gave her four yeses.

The yeses just kept coming when dance/acrobatic/free-running superstars OK Worldwide took to the stage and impressed the judges with their act, earning themselves four yeses and a place in the next round.

U.D.I were up next and they had a bit of a twist. The nine-strong dance troupe hail from Siberia where they use dance as a way to help the local orphanages, and if they win, they want to use the money to build a bigger school to continue their charity work.

It’s handy then, that they’re actually brilliant, and their light-display dancing wowed the judges.

David Walliams: “We always say here we’re looking for something we’ve never seen before on Britain’s Got Talent and I’ve never seen anything like that. Wow. Brilliant.”

Siberian dance troupe UDI's incredible neon display on Britain's Got Talent

Alesha Dixon: “Oh my goodness. Visually one of the best things I think I’ve ever seen. That was like absolutely perfect.”

Amanda Holden: “I’m almost at a loss for words. It just felt so brilliant.”

Simon Cowell: “Sometimes we’re asked why we have people from other countries entering but I’m so happy that we do have that because then we get to see artists as fantastic as you.”

Four yeses and a place in the next round came for them and then the luck ran out.

Mark Ponting, a 26-year-old supermarket assistant says he’s called ‘Mad Mark’ and his 80s style keytar performance got him buzzed off the stage.

Next up was liver reynolds, whose balloon trick music didn’t exactly go down well with the audience, who started chanting ‘off’ to him, and so he did.

Then, last and potentially least, was Alison Jiear, who’s spent years working as a background singer, but now she wants to step into the limelight.


Her rendition of You’ll Never Walk Alone was certainly powerful, but it didn’t seem to warm Simon Cowell’s icy heart.

Despite the audience becoming enraptured by the 49-year-old’s performance and giving her a standing ovation

Simon Cowell: “You know what? That was probably one of the best vocals we’ve ever had on this show because it was like, all the years of doing these commercials, being behind the scenes, getting frustrated and this was your one shot, and my God you took it.”

David Walliams: “We always say on this show, you’ve got two minutes to change your life and in that two minutes we saw a star being born tonight.”

Alesha Dixon: “That was mighty, it was magnificent, it was powerful. Great audition.”

Amanda Holden: “You’ve made some hugely brave decisions in your life and this was one of them coming on this stage and it’s paid off. That was an incredible, incredible audition so well done."

Unsurprisingly, Alison got four yeses, and let us leave this week's Britain’s Got Talent on a high.

resultats_lens.texte_contexte: Britain's Got Talent (5ème semaine) présente divers actes : le policier devenu drag queen Aaron Carty (imitant Beyoncé), Mitch et Cally the Wonderdog essayant de battre un record du monde de ballons éclatés, le fort the Victorian Strongman Daniel Crute (alias Leopold Aleksander) soulevant Amanda Holden, et Vladimir Georgievsky, un artiste de trampoline russe de 45 ans vivant à Swansea.
